solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Jerks pass out when cut by short sergeant-major

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been knocked from their proper order
a word cut by something is split open, with the cutter lodged in the gap

blocks.note: taken as written
SM is the standard abbreviation for sergeant-major, 'short' asking for it

explanation.surface: Soldiers keel over on the parade ground, interrupted by a curt sergeant-major barking at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' looks like fainting, or a passing-out parade, but 'out' only tells you to rearrange the word before the sergeant-major is lodged inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden involuntary muscle contractions, so the plural noun is a synonym for jerks or twitches.

clue.text: Far-right Katie, abandoning family, turns into a celeb

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters are dropped
turning into something else implies a change of form, so the remaining letters get rearranged

blocks.note: Katie Hopkins is a British media commentator known for hard-right opinions
kin are your relatives, your family

explanation.surface: A notorious right-wing pundit cuts ties with her relatives and reinvents herself as a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPKINS loses KIN to leave HOPS, which is rearranged. Posh Spice was Victoria Beckham's Spice Girls nickname, and she remains a celebrity under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh, the Spice Girls name of Victoria Beckham, is a famous person, hence a celebrity in the gossip-column sense.

clue.text: Dire supermarket clown

blocks.note: dire and grim both mean dreadful
Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A scathing review of a joker employed by a budget grocery store.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Grimaldi was a celebrated Regency-era English pantomime performer, so famous that clowns are still nicknamed Joeys after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimaldi is the most famous historical example of a circus and pantomime clown, the model for the white-faced comic.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Much depressed in the case of tweet-mad Trump?

definitions.text: Much depressed in the case of tweet-mad Trump?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone feeling very low and gloomy

blocks.clueFragment: in the case of tweet-mad Trump
blocks.note: setter's reading: a gadget whose touchscreen is pressed down constantly by a compulsive tweeter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' reads as sad, but here it is literal: pressed down, as screen buttons are, endlessly so by a president addicted to posting on Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern mobile handset with a touchscreen is the device used for posting messages, so it is constantly being pressed by its owner.

clue.text: Duels wrecked politician's rambling

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so its letters are broken and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician's aimless speech is spoiled by a string of combative exchanges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrecked' seems to describe the duels, but it only signals rearranging their letters before the Tory is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means lacking a plan or purpose and jumping between topics, the same sense as a wandering, aimless talk.

clue.text: Hack's to act in bad-tempered fashion

blocks.note: first meaning: to chop something crudely into pieces, describing the act literally
second meaning: a British idiom for turning angry or aggressive

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist is said to be prone to tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' invites the journalist, but it is the verb: hacking is cutting up roughly. The idiom 'cut up rough' is British for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut up rough is a colloquial phrase meaning to become quarrelsome, aggressive or violently angry, which is behaving with ill temper.

clue.text: Good girlie mag. for the non-working viewer

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl
Private Eye, the British satirical magazine in which this puzzle appears

explanation.surface: Recommending a racy magazine to readers who are out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girlie mag' suggests top-shelf reading, but the words split: girlie is LASS and the magazine is Private Eye itself, which hosts the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial eye fills a socket but cannot see, so it is an organ of sight that does not function.

clue.text: Agenda for GOP's main strike against Cyclops

indicators.note: the main part of a ship's sail or a head of something leads, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
the first letter of the abbreviation for the US Republican Party
to ram is to strike hard
Cyclops is the setter, so from the setter's point of view this is me

explanation.surface: The Republicans' plan of attack is chiefly aimed at this satirical crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself, so Cyclops gives ME. 'Against' is placement next to, not opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a planned list of items or proposals, just as an agenda sets out a schedule of business.

clue.text: Head's row reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to scull is to row a boat with oars

explanation.surface: Gossip about a quarrel involving the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like an argument, but it is the rowing sense, matching scull.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony case of the head, so the word is used loosely for the head itself.

clue.text: Approach an opportunity to get your leg over, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is spoken out, so the sound of the word is what counts

blocks.clueFragment: an opportunity to get your leg over
blocks.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Making a pass at someone in the hope of sex, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your leg over' is slang for having sex, but here it is literal: a stile lets walkers swing a leg over a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach and a style are both a characteristic manner or method of doing something.

clue.text: Boris finally the revolutionary? "Yours truly, right one to make a plan"

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the end of the name
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Is Boris Johnson secretly a revolutionary? A signed letter confesses he's the right man to plot it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted letter sign-off looks like dialogue, but each phrase is a separate piece: CHE, then ME, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer is a person who devises plots or plans, often in a crafty, underhand way.

clue.text: Out of bed, one's said to accompany 16 ac.?

blocks.note: someone out of bed is up
in the impersonal sense, one's belongs to you, so it is yours

explanation.surface: Someone climbing out of bed with a rude remark to go with a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is TWO-FINGER SALUTE, the British rude gesture; this vulgar retort is what people shout while making it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a crude British exclamation of contempt, often spoken while flicking the insulting V-sign at someone.

clue.text: Putin's head covered by old hat – fix

indicators.note: the head of anything is its top, so the opening letter is taken
something covered is wrapped in an outer layer, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the start of the Russian leader's name
old hat and stale both mean tired and unoriginal

explanation.surface: Putin wearing an antique hat, which ought to be repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat' seems to be the thing covering a head, but 'old hat' is a phrase for stale.
explanation.definitionFit: To staple papers is to fasten or attach them with a wire clip, a particular way of fixing things together.

clue.text: Poetical PC (Barking) on the rampage

indicators.note: a rampage is a wild, destructive spree, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police constable from the east London district of Barking goes on a lyrical spree.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is an east London district, and the brackets make it look like a police station address; it is the definition, as in barking mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking means raving or furious in British slang, and apoplectic describes someone overcome with rage, nearly bursting with fury.

clue.text: Patriotic figure way before a royal son

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Prince George is a son of the Prince of Wales

explanation.surface: A nationalist icon on the road ahead of a young prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince George is the eldest son of William, Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: St George, the dragon-slaying saint, is the patron of England, and his red cross flag is waved by patriots.

clue.text: Emerge – "ta" – with half of no bastard deal!

indicators.note: half a word is only part of it, so just one of its two letters is kept
a bastard version is a corrupted, impure form, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first of its two letters

explanation.surface: Brexit-era jeering: come out of the talks with a thank-you and only a partial no-deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No deal' was the Brexit slogan for leaving without a treaty; here the words are split, 'deal' alone being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal and an agreement are both a settled arrangement reached between parties, such as a trade treaty.

clue.text: Double-digit salary halved – Native Americans making dismissive gesture

indicators.note: cutting something in two throws away one half, so the back portion is discarded

blocks.note: a digit is a finger, so a double one is two fingers
taken as written, before its second half goes
the Ute are a Native American people of the Rocky Mountains

explanation.surface: Pay cut in half and turned into two figures, prompting a rude reaction from tribal workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-digit salary' reads as pay in the tens, but digit means finger. The two-finger salute is the British rude gesture, palm facing inward.
explanation.definitionFit: The V-sign made with the back of the hand outward is a British insult, an obscene signal of contempt.

clue.text: Descriptive  of Dolly, prime screen villain?

blocks.note: prime and top both mean best
a heavy is the bad guy or thug in a film

explanation.surface: Is Dolly cast as the chief baddie in a film?
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Parton, the country singer, is famous for her large bust; the question mark flags the cheeky definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-heavy means having more weight above than below, a teasing description of the famously buxom singer's figure.

clue.text: Early dictionary entry shows RADA's crappy (very) craft

indicators.note: something crappy is shoddily made, so the letters come out badly jumbled

blocks.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school
V is the abbreviation for very
Noah's Ark is a vessel, and a craft is a boat

explanation.surface: A drama school's terrible acting skills get a mention early in a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like the actor's skill, as in stagecraft, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginning with a double A, the African anteater's name comes near the very start of any English dictionary.

clue.text: Rubbed top of penis with processed oil drop

indicators.note: the top of a word in a row of letters is its first, so only that is used
processing changes raw material into another form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: its opening letter
taken as written
to shed is to let fall, to drop

explanation.surface: A smutty Private Eye image of lubricated self-pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately rude; 'drop' is the verb shed, as a tree drops leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish something is to rub it until it shines, so the past tense matches rubbed.

clue.text: Liberal given the boot by dictator Mark

indicators.note: someone given the boot is kicked out, so the letter is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
Joseph Stalin was the Soviet dictator

explanation.surface: A liberal-minded man named Mark is fired by a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' sits at the end like a person's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a discoloured spot or blemish, the same thing as a mark left on a surface.

clue.text: Showy thing from church, wearing Dior creation

indicators.note: whatever is worn is placed on the body, so one piece goes inside the clothing
a creation is something newly made, so the letters are fashioned into a fresh order

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flashy outfit at church, dressed in a designer couture gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creation' fits Dior as a fashion term for a designer gown, but here it signals rearranging the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are flowers prized for their striking, exotic and flamboyant blooms, so they are a showy plant.

clue.text: Balls up public school upbringing? That's mean!

indicators.note: a balls-up is a mess, and in a down clue up means turning the letters to read bottom to top

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school
ED is short for education, part of one's upbringing

explanation.surface: A rant that elite schooling ruins people and is downright nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as unkind, but it is the verb signify. A British public school is a fee-paying private school, Eton being the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or indicate, which is what a word or symbol does when it means something.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Late demand makes you cry

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner; late means former
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: An overdue bill or ultimatum reduces someone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry' looks like weeping but is shouting out.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to call out suddenly, so it is to cry in the sense of shouting with emotion.

clue.text: Perform sex with Joy – get much pleasure

blocks.note: to have someone is slang for sleeping with them
joy and fun both mean enjoyment

explanation.surface: Bedding a woman called Joy and thoroughly enjoying it.
explanation.walkthrough: Joy is capitalised to look like a woman's name, but it is just enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fun is the everyday idiom for enjoying yourself, deriving delight or amusement from an activity.

clue.text: It makes frock rock? Get away!

blocks.note: surface reading: something that livens up a dress or puts a party frock into a rock outfit
setter's reading: a curt expletive telling someone to leave, which literally strips the initial letter from the garment

explanation.walkthrough: Take the opening letter away from the dress and it becomes a stone; the instruction describing that removal is a familiar British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a euphemistic version of a coarse imperative telling someone to go away, a rude dismissal.

clue.text: Churchill's thing very sore at first before gin cocktail

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept
a cocktail is a mixed drink, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
its opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Churchill nursing a terrible hangover before his next gin drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Churchill famously flashed the V for victory in wartime photographs; turned round, the same sign is a British insult.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand signal with two fingers raised was Churchill's wartime trademark, his signature gesture of victory.

clue.text: Unlikely NF portion is charitable?

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement is an improbable one, so the letters take a new, unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Would any part of the National Front really be a charity? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: The NF is the National Front, a British far-right party, which makes 'charitable' look like irony.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-profit organisation exists for public good rather than earnings, which is the status of a charity.
